digest.definition: A broad, general study of organisations, their cultures, structures and management in economic, environmental and social context, rather than one function or sector
distinctiveFeatures: A broad, general study of organisations, their cultures, structures and management in economic, environmental and social context, rather than one function or sector
Organisations and business are read widely: public, private, non-profit, community and social enterprises of every size, from start-ups to global firms
Responsible leadership runs through it: values-led, inclusive, ethical and sustainable, with attention to climate change and net zero
Interdisciplinary and varied, drawing on the social sciences, humanities and sciences, with theory always set beside practice
Courses range from vocational study for business to research-oriented study of business, most combining the two
Strongly tied to practice and employability, through partnerships, placements, live projects and practitioner input
A dynamic, changing discipline whose courses are expected to keep innovating

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: framed through why, what and how the subject is taught: business education as a lever against inequality (with the SDGs), anti-discrimination law and inclusive workplaces as content, diverse cases including the Global South, and inclusive modes and assessment; reviewed with students (D1, 1.15 to 1.21)

regulatory minimum and whole-journey reach, reasonable adjustments in assessment, mindfulness of digital poverty and caring duties, and equal access to placements and international learning (D1, 1.22 to 1.24, 2.11, 2.12)

sustainable management as a condition of planetary survival, the SDGs and PRME, ethics, responsibility and sustainability (ERS) expected by some accreditors, carbon literacy and sustainable supply chains as example topics (D1, 1.25 to 1.28, 2.4)

entrepreneurship as a subject area and enterprise as a set of behaviours: venture creation, innovation inside established organisations, social enterprise and experiential learning; the front matter joins it with employability (D1, 1.29 to 1.33, 3.7, 3.10)

subjectSpecific.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can critically judge, what it means to manage responsibly and act ethically on social, cultural, legal, economic and environmental questions.
You should be able to show you understand how markets for resources, goods and services grow and work, including when they fail, their side effects and fair trade.

You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how organisations manage customers, how consumers behave, how markets are segmented and targeted, how sales are made and why products need innovation.
You should be able to show you understand where money for an organisation comes from, how it is managed, and how accounts and information systems help plan, control, decide and manage financial risk.

You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how people are led, managed and developed in organisations, how staff are engaged, what the law requires, and how culture and inclusion shape this.
You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how organisations manage resources, supply chains, buying, logistics, outsourcing, quality, service and projects.
You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how data, statistics and information systems are used in business and how they help organisations make decisions.

You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how organisations set policy and strategy in a changing world, manage risk and crises, keep going through disruption and communicate their plans.

You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how public services and voluntary and community organisations are run, funded, led and governed, and how they work with communities.

You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how new business ideas become products, services or organisations that pay back financially or socially, and why intellectual property matters.
You develop skills in managing people: communicating, building teams, looking after resilience and well-being, leading and motivating others, and making teams inclusive.
You develop skills in solving problems and analysing critically: working out what caused a problem, making decisions and choosing sustainable solutions.
You develop research skills: analysing and weighing up data, sources and methods, using digital tools well, and basing responsible, ethical decisions on the evidence.
You develop commercial sense: knowing what makes businesses succeed or fail and why keeping customers satisfied and loyal, in sustainable ways, matters.
You develop enterprise skills: coming up with and sharing ideas, protecting and using intellectual property, winning support and delivering lasting results.
You develop number skills: working with data and estimating, evaluating and modelling business problems.
You develop networking skills: listening well, negotiating, persuading and presenting, and using these to build business contacts.
You develop leadership skills: working across boundaries, influencing others, building relationships and partnering with other organisations and sectors.

transferable.text: You learn to work with others inclusively, both inside your organisation and beyond it.
You learn to communicate well in speech, through body language and online.
You learn to understand how others feel and to include them.
You learn to use digital tools well and to behave appropriately online.
You learn to think in concepts and systems, and critically: analysing, bringing ideas together and judging them.

You learn to manage yourself: learning independently, taking responsibility, staying flexible, coping with uncertainty and complexity, questioning assumptions, using evidence, bouncing back and speaking up when you need to.
You learn to reflect on yourself, to be aware of and sensitive to differences between people and cultures, and to keep wanting to grow.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: keeping innovation and variety in course design
statements.paraphrase: The statement is a broad, non-prescriptive frame for building and running courses; innovation, adaptability and variety mark the subject's courses, and that quality should be kept.

forPractitioner.text: Use the statement as a broad frame rather than a template: when you design or revise a course, the innovation, adaptability and variety typical of the subject should be kept.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design courses; it sets no outcome for the student

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: transferable skills for any career
statements.paraphrase: Skills and attributes here mean transferable academic and professional skills, suited to business careers but not confined to them; these skills will also prepare students to work well and responsibly as employees, colleagues, leaders and citizens of the world.

forPractitioner.text: Read skills and attributes as transferable academic and professional skills: they serve a business career and any other, and they will ready students to act effectively and responsibly at work, as leaders and as global citizens.

forBeneficiary.text: You will build academic and professional skills that carry over to any career, not only business, and that ready you to be an effective, responsible employee, colleague, leader and citizen of the world.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: the balance of purposes, shown in learning outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Courses cover the purposes in differing balance, which may follow what professional bodies ask for recognition; whatever balance a course strikes should be explainable and shown through its stated learning outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Decide how your course weights the four purposes in 1.4, noting any professional recognition that shapes it, and make that weighting explainable and visible in its specified learning outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team in writing outcomes

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: broad insight across business areas
statements.paraphrase: The subject's courses are marked by variety of content, interdisciplinarity and range of view; they are broad and should give insight into many areas of business, knowledge that carries into many settings.

forPractitioner.text: Keep the course broad: it should give students insight into a wide spread of business areas, drawing on varied content and disciplines so that what they learn carries into many settings.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should give you a view across many areas of business, not just one, so that what you learn can be used in many settings.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: a broad base for careers and further study
statements.paraphrase: The subject's courses lay a broad base from which students will be ready for many future careers and roles across organisations of every kind, and may lead on to postgraduate study in many specialisms.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course as a broad base: students will be ready for varied careers and roles in many kinds of organisation, and the course may also lead to specialist postgraduate study.

forBeneficiary.text: Your studies will give you a broad base for many kinds of career and role, in many kinds of organisation, and may lead on to postgraduate study in a specialism.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.appliesTo: the subject area and its courses
statements.about: EDI built into the culture and practice of the subject
statements.paraphrase: EDI covers many identity characteristics and kinds of difference, reaching past legal duties to intersections across students and staff; it should be a real concept built into the subject's culture and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Treat EDI as more than legal compliance: it should be a real presence in how the subject is taught and practised, attentive to intersecting identities among students and staff.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the subject community and course teams

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.appliesTo: future managers and leaders studying the subject
statements.about: EDI principles in future managers and leaders
statements.paraphrase: A focus on EDI lets business education help organisations tackle inequality and disadvantage, in line with the SDGs; joined with reflective practice it readies students for a diverse, global world, and study of the subject will instil EDI principles in future managers and leaders.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the subject so that EDI and reflective practice prepare students to work in a diverse, global world and to help organisations reduce inequality; the study will instil EDI principles in those who go on to manage and lead.

forBeneficiary.text: Your studies will build equality, diversity and inclusion into how you manage and lead, so that you can help organisations reduce inequality and do well in a diverse, global world.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.appliesTo: graduates and courses in the subject
statements.about: what is taught on EDI: law, inclusive workplaces, diverse content
statements.paraphrase: Courses make sure students critically grasp how organisations and their leaders advance EDI; graduates should know the legal duty to prevent discrimination and have the knowledge and skills to build inclusive workplaces; courses should also offer diverse content that questions dominant approaches, drawing on perspectives such as the Global South and marginalised communities.

forPractitioner.text: Teach a critical understanding of organisations' role in EDI; graduates should know anti-discrimination law and be able to foster inclusive workplaces; and the course content should be diverse, question dominant approaches and use cases that reflect the cohort and society.

forBeneficiary.text: You should come to understand the law against discrimination and gain the knowledge and skills to build inclusive workplaces; your course should also show you a wide range of perspectives and question the dominant ways the subject has been taught.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: inclusive design, teaching and modes of learning
statements.paraphrase: Courses should be built so that students of every background can reach their potential and feel represented; teaching and assessment should follow inclusive principles, with modes of learning chosen with care, and teaching should show awareness of EDI in its pedagogy.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course so students from all backgrounds can succeed and feel included; choose modes of learning and assessment designs with their different opportunities and barriers in mind, and let teaching approaches draw on the cohort's diversity.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design and teaching

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: EDI review as an ongoing process with students
statements.paraphrase: Attention to EDI is continuous: course teams should reflect regularly on improving it and, where they can, do so in partnership with students; changes to courses may include an equality impact assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Build EDI into regular course review: reflect on how to strengthen it, involve students as partners where possible, and consider an equality impact assessment when approving changes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course teams; students may take part as partners

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: accessibility meets regulation and covers the whole course
statements.paraphrase: At the least, accessibility should satisfy what regulation requires, and it will reach every stage of the course, from information before application to graduation and after.

forPractitioner.text: Make accessibility at least compliant with regulation and apply it end to end: pre-application information, teaching, assessment, graduation and beyond.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: equal access to work and international learning, and digital access
statements.paraphrase: Accessibility should give every student the same chances of workplace and international learning, and digital access that is inclusive and free of discrimination.

forPractitioner.text: Check that placements, work-based learning and study abroad are open to every student on equal terms, and that digital provision is inclusive and accessible.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: sustainability built into the curriculum across functions
statements.paraphrase: Managing for economic, social and environmental sustainability needs to run systematically through the curriculum and across business functions (the issuer's 'needs to', recorded as describes).

forPractitioner.text: Weave sustainability through the curriculum, in every functional area rather than one module, covering its economic, social and environmental sides.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on curriculum design

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: progression to threshold and readiness for postgraduate study
statements.paraphrase: An honours student will move from level to level under each institution's rules, each level building toward the threshold standards; a student reaching the typical standard or above would be expected to be ready for postgraduate study, though entry is for each provider to decide.

forPractitioner.text: Plan each level so attainment builds towards the threshold standards at FHEQ level 6 (FQHEIS level 10); students at typical or above would be expected to be ready for further study in the subject or a cognate one.

forBeneficiary.text: You will move up level by level, building towards at least the minimum standard for your honours degree; if you reach the typical standard or higher, you should be ready for postgraduate study, though each institution sets its own entry rules.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Business and Management degree

statements.appliesTo: students on joint, combined or major-minor routes
statements.about: core skills on joint and combined routes
statements.paraphrase: Students on combined, joint or major-minor routes will gain the core elements of the subject's specific and generic skills and add others from their second subject, possibly exploring where the two overlap.

forPractitioner.text: On joint and combined routes, ensure students will still reach the core specific and generic skills of the subject, and use the overlap with the second subject for interdisciplinary work.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study business and management alongside another subject, you will still gain its core skills, add skills from your other subject and may explore where the two meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Business and Management degree

statements.about: external reviewers in periodic review
statements.paraphrase: Externality is central to UK quality assurance: providers will bring in external reviewers during periodic review to gain an outside view of proposed changes and confirm that threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: Include external reviewers in periodic review so that proposed changes get an outside view and threshold standards and content are confirmed.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in review

statements.about: knowledge of organisations, their environment and governance
statements.paraphrase: Graduates should reasonably be able to show knowledge and understanding of varied organisations, their wider business setting and communities, and how they are governed and managed; courses stress the changing nature of work, the future of organisations globally, risk and their effect on society.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show they know and understand a range of organisations, their environment and governance; teach the changing nature of work, risk and organisations' impact on society.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show that you know and understand many kinds of organisation, the wider business world and communities around them, and how they are run and governed, including risk and their effect on society.

statements.appliesTo: successful graduates from every mode of learning
statements.about: integrating areas of understanding
statements.paraphrase: How areas of understanding relate and fit together matters greatly in the learning experience and should show in what successful graduates can do, whatever their mode of study.

forPractitioner.text: Build integration across areas into the course and its assessment; successful graduates from every mode should be able to show it.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show how the different areas of business you study connect and work together, whichever way you study.

statements.about: ethics, responsibility and sustainability
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of managing responsibly and acting ethically, above all on social, cultural, legal, economic and environmental questions.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate responsible management and ethical conduct across social, cultural, legal, economic and environmental issues.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can critically judge, what it means to manage responsibly and act ethically on social, cultural, legal, economic and environmental questions.

statements.about: markets and economies
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of how markets for resources, goods and services form, are reached and work, including market failure, externalities and fair trade.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate how markets develop and operate, with market failure, externalities and fair trade.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand how markets for resources, goods and services grow and work, including when they fail, their side effects and fair trade.

statements.about: marketing, sales, negotiation and customers
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of managing customer relationships, consumer behaviour, segmenting, targeting and positioning, selling and innovating in products and services.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate customer relationship management, consumer behaviour, segmentation, targeting and positioning, sales and product and service innovation.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how organisations manage customers, how consumers behave, how markets are segmented and targeted, how sales are made and why products need innovation.

statements.about: finance and accounting
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of where finance comes from, how it is managed, and how accounting and other information systems support planning, control, decisions and financial risk.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate where finance comes from and how it is managed, and how accounting and information systems serve planning, control, decisions and financial risk.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand where money for an organisation comes from, how it is managed, and how accounts and information systems help plan, control, decide and manage financial risk.

statements.about: people, organisational behaviour and EDI
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of responsible, inclusive and ethical leadership, managing and developing people and organisations, employee engagement and employment law, grounded in cross-cultural understanding and EDI.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate inclusive, ethical leadership, people management and development, engagement and the legal context, with cross-cultural and EDI understanding.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how people are led, managed and developed in organisations, how staff are engaged, what the law requires, and how culture and inclusion shape this.

statements.about: operations and business innovation
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of managing resources, supply chains, procurement, logistics, outsourcing, quality systems, service excellence and projects.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate operations: resources, supply chain, procurement, logistics, outsourcing, quality, service and project management.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how organisations manage resources, supply chains, buying, logistics, outsourcing, quality, service and projects.

statements.about: data, digital business and information systems
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of setting strategic priorities for fast delivery through managing and applying information systems, their effect on organisations, and data-led decisions.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate data analytics, statistics, digital business and information systems, their organisational impact and data-driven decision-making.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how data, statistics and information systems are used in business and how they help organisations make decisions.

statements.about: business policy and strategy
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of forming policies and strategies for a changing setting and stakeholder interests, with risk and crisis management, continuity planning and communication used to reach strategic aims.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate how policies and strategies are developed for changing environments, with risk, crisis, continuity and communication methods.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how organisations set policy and strategy in a changing world, manage risk and crises, keep going through disruption and communicate their plans.

statements.about: public and non-profit management
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of what is distinct in public service bodies and the voluntary and community sector: governance, finance, public leadership, community empowerment, coproduction, public value and hybrid delivery.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate public and non-profit management: governance, finance, leadership, empowerment, coproduction, public values and hybrid service delivery.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how public services and voluntary and community organisations are run, funded, led and governed, and how they work with communities.

statements.about: entrepreneurship and enterprise development
statements.paraphrase: Should show knowledge and critical evaluation of turning new business ideas into products, services or organisations that return financial or social value, including spotting intellectual property and valuing it.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show and critically evaluate how new ventures, products and services are created for financial or social return, including intellectual property.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show you understand, and can judge critically, how new business ideas become products, services or organisations that pay back financially or socially, and why intellectual property matters.

statements.about: cognitive, subject-specific, personal and interpersonal skills
statements.paraphrase: Graduates should be able to show cognitive and intellectual skills with competencies particular to business and management, and also personal and interpersonal skills, both subject-specific and generic.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should be able to show intellectual skills and business competencies, and personal and interpersonal skills; plan for subject-specific and generic skills alike (listed in 3.10 and 3.11).

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to show thinking skills and business competencies, and personal and interpersonal skills, both specific to business and useful anywhere.

statements.about: people management
statements.paraphrase: People management: communicating, building teams, resilience and well-being, leading and motivating, and fostering EDI.

forPractitioner.text: Develop people management: communication, team building, resilience and well-being, leading and motivating others, and nurturing EDI.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop skills in managing people: communicating, building teams, looking after resilience and well-being, leading and motivating others, and making teams inclusive.

statements.about: problem-solving and critical analysis
statements.paraphrase: Problem-solving and critical analysis: examining facts and circumstances to find a problem's cause, then deciding on fitting, sustainable solutions.

forPractitioner.text: Develop problem-solving and critical analysis: diagnosing causes from facts and circumstances, then deciding on sustainable solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop skills in solving problems and analysing critically: working out what caused a problem, making decisions and choosing sustainable solutions.

statements.about: research and evidence-based decisions
statements.paraphrase: Research: analysing and judging data, information sources and suitable methods, with strong digital literacy, and using the findings for decisions that are evidence-based, responsible and ethical.

forPractitioner.text: Develop research skills: analysing and evaluating data, sources and methods, with strong digital literacy, and applying findings to responsible, ethical, evidence-based decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop research skills: analysing and weighing up data, sources and methods, using digital tools well, and basing responsible, ethical decisions on the evidence.

statements.about: commercial acumen
statements.paraphrase: Commercial acumen: grounded in awareness of what drives business success and failure, and why customer satisfaction and loyalty matter, pursued sustainably.

forPractitioner.text: Develop commercial acumen: awareness of the drivers of success, causes of failure, and sustainable customer satisfaction and loyalty.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop commercial sense: knowing what makes businesses succeed or fail and why keeping customers satisfied and loyal, in sustainable ways, matters.

statements.about: innovation, creativity and enterprise
statements.paraphrase: Innovation, creativity and enterprise: acting entrepreneurially to produce, develop and share ideas, handle and use intellectual property, win support and achieve sustainable results.

forPractitioner.text: Develop innovation, creativity and enterprise: entrepreneurial action to generate and communicate ideas, manage intellectual property, gain backing and deliver sustainable outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop enterprise skills: coming up with and sharing ideas, protecting and using intellectual property, winning support and delivering lasting results.

statements.about: numeracy and quantitative skills
statements.paraphrase: Numeracy: using quantitative skills to work with data and to judge, estimate and model the problems and functions of a business.

forPractitioner.text: Develop numeracy: quantitative skills to handle data and to evaluate, estimate and model business problems.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop number skills: working with data and estimating, evaluating and modelling business problems.

statements.about: networking and interpersonal skills
statements.paraphrase: Networking: awareness of listening, negotiating, persuading and presenting, and using them to build business contacts.

forPractitioner.text: Develop networking: listening, negotiation, persuasion and presentation used to cultivate business contacts.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop networking skills: listening well, negotiating, persuading and presenting, and using these to build business contacts.

statements.about: boundary-spanning and collaborative leadership
statements.paraphrase: Leadership: spanning boundaries, influencing, relating and collaborating, including partnership working across organisations and sectors.

forPractitioner.text: Develop leadership: boundary-spanning, influence, relational and collaborative work and partnership across organisations and sectors.

forBeneficiary.text: You develop leadership skills: working across boundaries, influencing others, building relationships and partnering with other organisations and sectors.

statements.about: collaborative and inclusive working
statements.paraphrase: Working together, inclusively, with stakeholders inside and outside the organisation.

forPractitioner.text: Develop collaborative, inclusive working with internal and external stakeholders.

forBeneficiary.text: You learn to work with others inclusively, both inside your organisation and beyond it.

statements.about: verbal, non-verbal and digital communication
statements.paraphrase: Communicating in speech, without words and through digital means.

forPractitioner.text: Develop verbal, non-verbal and digital communication.

forBeneficiary.text: You learn to communicate well in speech, through body language and online.

statements.about: empathy and inclusivity
statements.paraphrase: Empathy and inclusivity.

forPractitioner.text: Develop empathy and inclusivity.

forBeneficiary.text: You learn to understand how others feel and to include them.

statements.about: digital literacy and etiquette
statements.paraphrase: Using digital tools capably and behaving appropriately online.

forPractitioner.text: Develop digital literacy and appropriate digital conduct.

forBeneficiary.text: You learn to use digital tools well and to behave appropriately online.

statements.about: conceptual, systemic and critical thinking
statements.paraphrase: Conceptual, systems and critical thinking, with analysis, synthesis and evaluation.

forPractitioner.text: Develop thinking that is conceptual, systemic and critical, with analysis, synthesis and evaluation.

forBeneficiary.text: You learn to think in concepts and systems, and critically: analysing, bringing ideas together and judging them.

statements.about: self-management and independent learning
statements.paraphrase: Self-management: growing as an independent learner, ready to take responsibility, be flexible, live with uncertainty, handle complexity, question assumptions, think critically from evidence, and be resilient, self-starting and suitably assertive.

forPractitioner.text: Develop self-management: independent learning, responsibility, flexibility, tolerance of uncertainty, handling complexity, challenging assumptions, evidence-led critical thinking, resilience and appropriate assertiveness.

forBeneficiary.text: You learn to manage yourself: learning independently, taking responsibility, staying flexible, coping with uncertainty and complexity, questioning assumptions, using evidence, bouncing back and speaking up when you need to.

statements.about: self-reflection and sensitivity to diversity
statements.paraphrase: Self-reflection: analysing oneself, awareness of and sensitivity to differences between people and cultures, and a lasting wish to develop.

forPractitioner.text: Develop self-reflection: self-analysis, sensitivity to diversity in people and cultures, and continuing appetite for development.

forBeneficiary.text: You learn to reflect on yourself, to be aware of and sensitive to differences between people and cultures, and to keep wanting to grow.

statements.about: assessment for learning and timely, usable feedback
statements.paraphrase: Assessment should be part of learning, helped by feedback on formative and summative work; feedback should come in good time and be usable, supporting development within a module and across the course.

forPractitioner.text: Make assessment part of learning: give feedback on formative and summative work, promptly and in a form students can act on within the module and across the course.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who set and mark assessment

statements.about: reliable, inclusive and varied assessment methods
statements.paraphrase: Assessment methods need to assess the intended outcomes reliably and be inclusively designed (the issuer's 'need to', recorded as describes), and may also be varied, new and skill-building in themselves.

forPractitioner.text: Choose assessment methods that reliably test the intended outcomes and are inclusive by design; they can also be varied and innovative and build skills in their own right.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design assessment

statements.about: extent, fit and marking of group work
statements.paraphrase: When assessment is done in groups, care should go into how much group work a course has, how authentic and suited to its task it is, and how marks are split between group and individual.

forPractitioner.text: Weigh the amount of group assessment across the course, its authenticity and fit to the task, and how group and individual marks are attributed.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on assessment design

statements.about: guidance and weighting limits for peer assessment
statements.paraphrase: Peer review and assessment can engage students in assessment and learning; whether formative or summative, students should get clear guidance and the weight of peer marks in a unit or module should be capped.

forPractitioner.text: When using peer assessment, give students clear guidance and cap the weight of peer marks in a module.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on assessment design

statements.about: transparent assessment and shared marking criteria
statements.paraphrase: Assessment details should be open and given to students with the marking criteria; students may also co-design assessments with tutors or peers.

forPractitioner.text: Share assessment details and marking criteria with students openly, and consider co-designing assessments with them.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team; students meet its effect

statements.about: assessment designed with workload in mind
statements.paraphrase: Assessment design should take account of how much work students carry.

forPractitioner.text: Plan assessment with the student's whole workload in view, across modules and deadlines.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on assessment design

statements.about: most exceed threshold; refer to Annex D for degree classes
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do much better than the minimum threshold; each provider decides what evidence shows achievement and should refer to Annex D, which describes the four honours classes (1st, 2.1, 2.2, 3rd) for FHEQ level 6 and FQHEIS level 10.

forPractitioner.text: Set your own evidence of achievement, but refer to Annex D's descriptions of the four honours classes; expect most students to perform well above the threshold.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in setting classification evidence

statements.about: threshold as minimum, typical as the expected norm
statements.paraphrase: Three categories, threshold, typical and excellent, set apart graduates' achievement and rest on perceived national norms in the subject; threshold is the minimum for all honours graduates, and most students should reach typical.

forPractitioner.text: Use the three categories for individual performance: threshold is the floor for every honours graduate, and most students should reach the typical standard.

forBeneficiary.text: If you complete an honours degree you will have reached at least the minimum standard, and, like most students, you should reach the typical standard.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold rung
statements.about: key areas, their relationships and application
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown knowledge and understanding of the main areas of business and management, how they relate and how they are applied.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have shown they know and understand the key areas of the subject, how they interrelate and how they apply.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will have shown that you know and understand the main areas of business and management, how they link and how they are used.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold rung
statements.about: competence across subject-specific and generic skills
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence across the subject's own skills and its generic skills and attributes.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have shown competence across the subject-specific and generic skills and attributes.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will have shown that you are competent in the range of business skills and general skills.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold rung
statements.about: a mainly guided view with some critical perspective
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown a view of the subject shaped mostly by guided learning, with some sign of a critical stance.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will hold a view of the subject formed largely through guided learning, with some evidence of critical perspective.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, your view of business will come mostly from what you have been guided to learn, with some signs that you question it.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold rung
statements.about: applying knowledge in a current organisational setting
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the skills and abilities to use knowledge in a present-day organisational setting.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have shown they can apply their knowledge in a contemporary organisation.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will have shown that you can use what you know in a present-day organisation.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold rung
statements.about: practising global social responsibility
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to act on the values of global social responsibility.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have shown a capacity to practise global social responsibility.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum standard, you will have shown that you can put the values of global social responsibility into practice.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical rung
statements.about: solid knowledge of a broad range and complex relationships
statements.paraphrase: Will typically have shown solid, substantial knowledge and understanding across a broad range of business and management areas, the complex links between them and how they are applied in practice.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical rung, graduates will usually have shown solid, substantial knowledge across many areas, their complex interrelations and their use in practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will usually have shown solid, substantial knowledge across a broad range of business areas, the complex ways they link and how they work in practice.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical rung
statements.about: command of subject skills, proficiency in generic skills
statements.paraphrase: Will typically have shown command of subject-specific skills and proficiency in generic skills and attributes.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical rung, graduates will usually have shown command of the subject's skills and proficiency in generic ones.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will usually have shown command of business skills and real proficiency in general skills.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical rung
statements.about: a view drawn from wide sources, with independence and critical evaluation
statements.paraphrase: Will typically have shown a view of the subject drawn from a wide range of fitting sources, with evidence of independent learning and critical evaluation.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical rung, graduates will usually have a view informed by wide, appropriate sources, showing independent learning and critical evaluation.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, your view of business will usually draw on many suitable sources, showing that you learn independently and judge critically.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical rung
statements.about: applying knowledge in complex settings, with own perspectives
statements.paraphrase: Will typically have shown the ability to use knowledge in complex, current organisational settings, and some capacity to form and use their own views, handle uncertainty and complexity, look at alternative answers, evaluate critically and bring theory in.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical rung, graduates will usually apply knowledge in complex organisations and show some capacity for their own perspective, coping with uncertainty, weighing alternatives, critical evaluation and integrating theory.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will usually be able to use what you know in complex organisations, and show some ability to form your own views, cope with uncertainty, weigh up alternatives, judge critically and draw on theory.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical rung
statements.about: integrating global social responsibility
statements.paraphrase: Will typically have shown the ability to build the values of global social responsibility into their work.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical rung, graduates will usually have shown they can integrate the values of global social responsibility.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will usually have shown that you can build the values of global social responsibility into what you do.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the excellent rung
statements.about: advanced, critical knowledge and detailed relationships
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown advanced knowledge and critical understanding across a broad range of business and management areas, the detailed links between them and their application in practice.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent rung, graduates will have shown advanced knowledge and critical understanding of many areas, their detailed interrelations and their use in practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have shown advanced knowledge and a critical grasp of a broad range of business areas, the detailed ways they link and how they apply in practice.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the excellent rung
statements.about: excellent command of subject skills, proficiency in generic skills
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown excellent command of subject-specific skills and proficiency in generic skills and attributes.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent rung, graduates will have shown excellent command of the subject's skills and proficiency in generic ones.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have shown excellent command of business skills and real proficiency in general skills.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the excellent rung
statements.about: a proactive, independent view that challenges assumptions
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown a view of the subject built from analysing wide sources, through proactive, independent learning that challenges assumptions and questions the status quo.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent rung, graduates will hold a view formed by analysing wide sources, learning proactively and independently, challenging assumptions and questioning accepted practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, your view of business will come from analysing many sources, learning on your own initiative, challenging assumptions and questioning the way things are done.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the excellent rung
statements.about: exceptional own perspective and integration of theory and practice
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown exceptional ability to form and use their own views, handle uncertainty and complexity, look at alternative answers, evaluate critically and join theory with practice in many situations.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent rung, graduates will have shown exceptional capacity for their own perspective, for uncertainty and complexity, alternatives, critical evaluation and integrating theory and practice widely.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have shown an exceptional ability to form your own views, cope with uncertainty and complexity, weigh up alternatives, judge critically and join theory with practice in many situations.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the excellent rung
statements.about: championing global social responsibility while weighing its debates
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the ability to challenge assumptions and champion global social responsibility while recognising the debates and conflicting views it raises in complex business settings.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent rung, graduates will have shown they can challenge assumptions and champion global social responsibility while appreciating its debates and tensions in complex settings.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have shown that you can challenge assumptions and champion global social responsibility, while seeing the debates and disagreements it raises in complex business settings.
